rows.subject: direct submit_proposal, commit durably succeeds then raises: caller-visible class + exact message
rows.method: Injected a sqlite3.Connection factory through store_module.sqlite3.connect; a CREATE TEMP TABLE write transaction proved one intercepted commit, then commit() called super().commit(), returned, and raised sqlite3.OperationalError. Captured the public call result after Store.transaction closed.
rows.verdict: A durable direct submission can raise StateError and return no proposal ID.

rows.subject: direct: requests/proposals/events row deltas measured AFTER the raising commit returns
rows.method: Counted every non-sqlite_% table discovered from sqlite_schema on separate connections before injection and after the raised commit; subtracted all 13 counts.
rows.verdict: The raising commit durably adds exactly one request, proposal, and event and changes no other application table.

rows.subject: direct: does the caller receive any proposal id, and is the minted id discoverable at all
rows.method: Patched uuid.uuid4 to deterministic values, attempted direct submission, then opened a separate connection after the raise and queried requests(id, proposal_id) and proposals(id).
rows.verdict: The caller gets no ID, but the minted proposal ID remains discoverable in the durable request/proposal binding.

rows.subject: source propose, same injected commit: class, message and the same three row deltas
rows.method: Used the live-controlled Connection factory on System.propose after a one-commit positive control. The source returned one deterministic candidate, commit() called super().commit() and then raised, and a separate post-raise connection counted every live application table.
rows.verdict: Source-backed submission has the same uncertainty window and durable three-row footprint as direct submission.

rows.subject: recovery route: does system.proposals(partition, status='pending') surface the orphan row
rows.method: After the direct call raised, removed the injected factory and called system.proposals('tenant_a', status='pending') through a fresh read transaction; projected each returned id, request_id, and status.
rows.verdict: The pending feed surfaces the orphan and both durable IDs, providing the operator's discovery route.

rows.subject: recovery route: does get_proposal(partition, id) resolve the orphan once its id is known
rows.method: Took the orphan proposal id from durable storage, then called system.get_proposal('tenant_a', id) through an ordinary fresh read transaction and recorded the returned ProposalView fields.
rows.verdict: Once its ID is known, get_proposal fully resolves the orphan and reveals its bound request and candidate content.

rows.subject: recovery route: can an operator bind the orphan proposal back to its requests row
rows.method: Compared the proposal and request IDs exposed by proposals(status='pending') and get_proposal with a separate-connection JOIN of proposals.request_id to requests.id and the reciprocal requests.proposal_id binding.
rows.verdict: The public recovery reads expose the exact request ID, and the durable rows bind both IDs reciprocally.

rows.subject: CONTROL, commit that does not raise: the same observables on an ordinary success
rows.method: Ran the same deterministic direct submission through the same live-proved Connection factory in pass mode, then captured its return and counted every live application table from a separate connection.
rows.verdict: Ordinary success has the same durable footprint but returns the exact stored proposal ID and raises nothing.

rows.subject: is the window submission-specific, or does System.handle exhibit it identically
rows.method: MAIN-derived. Same injected `sqlite3.Connection` whose `commit()` calls `super().commit()` and then raises `OperationalError`, applied to `System.handle` on a registered operation. Deltas read from a separate connection over all 13 derived application tables.
rows.observed: `StateError: database is busy or unavailable`, delta `{requests: 1}` durable. Identical class and message to the submission window; the row count differs only because `handle` writes a different row set.
rows.verdict: The window is NOT submission-specific. `handle` exhibits it identically, so the property belongs to `Store.transaction`, not to M3.3's methods.
rows.reproduction: See the W10/W11 probe recorded in the M3.3 S4 commit body; the injection is the same factory the committed test `test_a_commit_that_succeeds_then_raises_leaves_the_rows_durable` installs.

rows.subject: does a non-submission writer (register_operation or review) exhibit it identically
rows.method: MAIN-derived. Same injection applied to `System.register_operation`, a non-submission writer on a fresh ledger.
rows.observed: `StateError: database is busy or unavailable`, delta `{operations: 1, events: 1}` durable.
rows.verdict: A non-submission writer exhibits the identical window, confirming W10: every method that commits through `Store.transaction` shares it. Scoping it inside M3.3's candidate boundary would misattribute a seam property.
rows.reproduction: Same probe as W10, with `register_operation` as the action.

rows.subject: any observable separating commit-raised-after-durability from commit-raised-before-durability
rows.method: MAIN-derived control pair, now the committed pin's second half: the identical injection run twice, once raising after `super().commit()` and once not, with deltas compared over all 13 derived application tables.
rows.observed: raise-after-commit -> `StateError`, returned `None`, delta `{requests:1, proposals:1, events:1}`. no-raise control -> returned a `prop_` id, delta `{requests:1, proposals:1, events:1}`. The two deltas are EQUAL; the full row set is the same shape and the same content.
rows.verdict: NO observable available to the caller in the ledger separates commit-raised-after-durability from an ordinary success. Only the caller's own return-vs-raise differs, and that is exactly the signal the failing caller cannot trust. This is why the published recovery route is content matching over the partition's pending proposals and never a retry.
rows.reproduction: `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_submission.SubmissionTests.test_a_commit_that_succeeds_then_raises_leaves_the_rows_durable` - its control half asserts the equality directly.
